text:
Mikael Granlund is 34, on his sixth NHL team, and scoring at a far better rate than last season: 24 points in 20 games after 41 in 58 last season. Eleven of those points came on Anaheim's power play, and 16 came in his last ten games, well above the 10.2 our numbers expected.

Here is the catch. At five on five the Ducks have been outchanced badly with him on the ice, holding just 42.7% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they're worse with him than without him. What's keeping his points up is the finishing around him: Anaheim has scored 9.1 more goals than those chances deserve with him on the ice, and his own shooting at 18.9% is above the top of our range for him. On-ice luck like that fades. The playmaking is real, and Evolving-Hockey had him driving chances well last season (90th percentile among forwards), but our range for his scoring rate sits well under where it is now. We'd watch the five-on-five share: it's the part of his game that decides whether this pace is real.
